blocks.name: 4-Week Foundation Block

weeks.label: Foundation
weeks.focus: Learn the hinge and squat patterns with kettlebells at 2 to 3 reps in reserve on every set. Establish the Monday, Wednesday, Friday rhythm and record the four baselines.

weeks.label: Foundation +
weeks.focus: Same movements. Move to a slightly heavier bell only on exercises where every rep last week was controlled. Soreness should be fading, not building.

weeks.label: Build
weeks.focus: The barbell Romanian deadlift enters, empty or lightly loaded. Goblet squats and deadlifts add a set. Kettlebell swings unlock only if the hinge looks solid.

weeks.label: Consolidate
weeks.focus: Hold week 3 loads and sharpen form. Finish every session feeling strong, then retest the four baselines at the end of the week.

blocks.intro: A phase-in month for a strong, generally fit body that has not been under a barbell or kettlebell program in a while. Years of ski racing built powerful quads; this block deliberately balances that with posterior chain and back work: deadlifts, Romanian deadlifts, rows, carries, and direct trunk work, because a desk job and a quad-dominant history both leave the back of the body underfed. Rowing appears in every session but is capped at 10 minutes. The goal of the month is not to lift heavy. It is to leave week 4 with clean patterns, a resilient back, and room to progress cleanly into the next block.
rules: Every set ends with 2 to 3 reps left in the tank. This month is for learning patterns, not testing strength.
Three sessions a week with at least one full rest day between them. If a session is missed, shift the week; never stack two training days back to back to catch up.
Move up in kettlebell weight only when every rep of every set was controlled at the target reps. "Felt easy" is a green light for next week, not for the next set.
The barbell Romanian deadlift stays light all month. An empty bar is plenty for many people at first; two kettlebells work if the bar feels heavy.
Sharp pain, especially in the low back, ends that movement for the day. Substitute the easier variation listed and make a note.
Soreness that changes how you walk means the next session runs lighter, not skipped.
recovery: Eating pattern: three meals a day, each with a palm-sized-or-larger protein portion (~30–40 g). The meal within an hour after training is the one that matters most — protein plus carbohydrate. No calorie targets in this block; the goal is patterns and consistency, not a deficit.

Water: ~2.5 L on training days, ~2 L on rest days — tea, milk, and sparkling water count. Adult-female adequate intake is ~2.7 L/day total with about a fifth from food; altitude and dry air push it up. Pale-straw urine by mid-morning is the check; forcing water past clear does nothing useful.
Sleep 7.5 hours or more. Strength at this stage is built between sessions, not during them.
Hamstring and glute soreness in weeks 1 and 2 is normal and fades. Low back tightness that lingers past a day is the signal to lighten the next hinge day.
Off days are for easy movement: walks, easy spins, gentle stretching. Nothing that leaves you sore.
tests: Goblet squat: bell weight that feels controlled for 8 reps
Ring row: body angle for 8 clean reps (note where the feet are)

rest.label: Rest
rest.note: Easy movement is welcome; hard effort is not.

warmup.title: Warm-up
warmup.subtitle: Every training day · before the main work

items.name: Easy row
items.detail: 4 min at a fully conversational effort.

items.name: Circuit × 2
items.detail: 10 bodyweight squats · 10 band pull-aparts · 8 unloaded hip hinges (dowel on the back or hands on hips, push the hips back to a hamstring stretch, flat back throughout). Hinge drill linked; band pull-aparts: youtu.be/Xg58d9lDWME

items.name: Before
items.detail: 12–16 oz water with a pinch of salt on waking — Driggs is dry and high, and thirst under-reports here. Train fasted if that feels normal, or eat a light breakfast (yogurt + fruit) 60–90 min before. Either is fine at this intensity.

items.name: Within 60 min after
items.detail: The recovery meal. Breakfast or lunch depending on when you trained: a solid protein serving (eggs + Greek yogurt, or a whey shake with milk and fruit, or a chicken/fish plate) plus carbohydrate. This is the meal that matters most for the block.

items.name: Protein at every meal
items.detail: Three meals, each with a palm-sized-or-larger protein portion (roughly 30–40 g). Spread across the day beats one big dose. No counting required — the palm rule at each meal gets there.

items.name: Water
items.detail: ~2.5 L (85 oz) of fluids on training days, ~2 L (70 oz) otherwise — water, tea, milk, sparkling water all count. The adult-female adequate intake is ~2.7 L/day total with about a fifth from food, and altitude adds to it. Easiest pattern: a glass on waking, one during the session, one with each meal. Check: pale-straw urine by mid-morning. Do not force water past clear urine.

items.name: Sleep
items.detail: 7.5+ hours. Strength at this stage is built between sessions, not during them.

items.name: Kettlebell deadlift
items.detail: Bell between the feet, hips back, flat back, stand tall. The pattern of the whole month.

byWeek.2: 3×8, slightly heavier bell only if every week 1 rep was controlled.

items.name: Barbell Romanian deadlift
items.detail: Bar slides down the thighs to the deepest flat-back range, then hips drive forward. Pattern quality over load; an empty bar or two kettlebells is plenty.

items.name: Ring row
items.detail: Body in one line, squeeze the shoulder blades, pull the rings to the ribs. Walk the feet forward to make it harder, back to make it easier.

byWeek.3: 3×8–10, lower the body angle a step.

items.name: Single-arm kettlebell row
items.detail: Free hand braced on the rack or a bench, flat back, pull the bell to the hip.

items.name: Medicine ball chest pass or slam
items.detail: Full-body and fast. Chest pass against a wall, or slam to the floor.

items.name: Glute bridge
items.detail: Squeeze at the top for a full second; ribs down, no low-back arch.

items.name: Single-leg glute bridge
items.detail: Hips stay level; drive through the heel.

items.name: Dead bug
items.detail: Low back gently pressed to the floor the entire time. Slow, opposite arm and leg.

liftb.title: Lift B
liftb.subtitle: Squat + press · legs, shoulders, upper back

items.name: Goblet squat
items.detail: Bell at the chest, elbows inside the knees at the bottom, chest tall.

byWeek.2: 3×8, heavier bell if week 1 was controlled.

items.name: Half-kneeling kettlebell press
items.detail: One knee down, glute of the down leg squeezed, press without leaning back.

items.name: Kettlebell reverse lunge
items.detail: Step back, knee toward the floor with control, drive up through the front heel. Balance work for a ski racer's side-to-side symmetry.

byWeek.1: 3×6 per leg, bodyweight or a light bell held goblet style.
byWeek.3: 3×8 per leg, add or increase the bell.

items.name: Band good morning
items.detail: Band over the shoulders and under the feet; hinge against it with a flat back.

items.name: Kettlebell swing
items.detail: Only if the hinge looks solid. Hips snap, arms relax, bell floats to chest height. Otherwise repeat band good mornings.

items.name: Band face pull
items.detail: Band anchored at eye level on the rack; pull to the face with elbows high and wide. Desk-job antidote.

items.name: Farmer carry
items.detail: A bell in each hand, tall posture, no leaning.

items.name: Suitcase carry
items.detail: One bell only, switch sides each trip; resist the sideways lean. Quiet, honest trunk work.

items.name: Bird dog
items.detail: Opposite arm and leg, hips level, slow. Reach long rather than high.

items.name: Pacing
items.detail: Moderate means short phrases are possible, not gasping. Legs drive, arms finish; the damper does not need to be high.

liftc.title: Lift C
liftc.subtitle: Mixed strength · hinge volume, push, rotation

items.name: Kettlebell Romanian deadlift
items.detail: Bell slides down the thighs with a 2 to 3 second lowering; soft knees, flat back, hamstring stretch at the bottom.

items.name: Kettlebell deadlift
items.detail: Heavier than the weeks 1 and 2 bell; every rep crisp.

items.name: Incline push-up
items.detail: Hands on the rack safety bar. Body in one rigid line; lower the bar setting over time, not the standards.

items.name: Medicine ball rotational toss
items.detail: Against a wall or to a partner. Power comes from the hips turning, not the arms.

items.name: Band lateral walk
items.detail: Band around the legs above the knees, quarter squat, steady steps sideways. Hip stability for lunges and for skiing.

items.name: Side plank
items.detail: Elbow under the shoulder, hips tall in one line.

items.name: Walk
items.detail: 20 to 30 minutes at a genuinely easy pace, outside if the weather allows.

items.name: Gentle stretch
items.detail: A few minutes for whatever feels tight: hamstrings, hips, chest. Nothing forced.

items.name: Meals
items.detail: Same three meals with a palm-sized protein portion each. Rest days are where the muscle actually gets built — do not skip protein because there was no session.

items.name: Water
items.detail: ~2 L (70 oz) of fluids; tea, milk, and sparkling water count. Pale-straw urine by mid-morning is the check. Thirst is a reasonable guide on rest days; the number exists because a dry climate blunts it.
